items.subject: Give it everything you've got
items.summary: Sister Heintzelman shares her busy final weeks as a missionary, a baptism, and her upcoming homecoming.
items.body:
Apparently when you try to avoid talking or thinking about your mission ending, everyone else gets the exact opposite idea. Every member and missionary that I know has been asking me about going home and my last meals.

We had a very busy week. Highlights:
- A very sweet and tender talk with Hermana Pineda
- Spanish exchange with Sister McDonald in La Joya. The friend we taught, Cesar, got baptized on Sunday!
- An awesome lesson with Gabriel, Neydy, and two of their kids.
- Brenda has been reading her Book of Mormon. Please pray for her.
- The funniest lesson with Cesar about the word of wisdom.
- We finally got to have a lesson with some members of the Cano family.

Hardest point of this week was when our dear friend Maria decided she would no longer come to church or be baptized.

All in all this week has been full of love, laughter, and growth. I'm giving it everything I've got and laying it all out on the field.

I want you all to know that God can make the most beautiful garden out of your worst desert. The joy comes in doing the work not in seeing the results. Trust Him, His plan and timing.

May God be with you all til we meet again.

Sister Heintzelman

Also if you want the information for my arrival and my homecoming, go ahead and reach out!

items.subject: Great and dreadful day pt2
items.summary: Brysen updates everyone from Africa: same area and companion, moving apartments, plus a thought on keeping your testimony after the mission.
items.body:
Hey everyone hows life going? The work of the Lord is still booming for me down here in Africa.

For now, let's talk about transfers. I am staying in the same area with the same companion, which I am very much not mad at all about. Here's where things get interesting: I am moving apartments. My next home is an apartment that the church just bought, so who knows what it's gonna be like. I don't have official transfer news yet, so I don't know who my new roommates will be.

Spiritual thought:

On Tuesday we had the opportunity to hear a devotional from Elder Morrison of the 70. He began by talking about testimonies, and how if we are not actively working to grow or protect them the devil will begin to break them. As important as spiritual experiences are that build your testimony, it's almost more important what happens after. Do you allow yourself to become better because of it or go back to how you were before?

So when you have a testimony building experience, make sure you continue to maintain and build what you gained, otherwise it will have been for nothing.

Love yall and have a great week!

items.subject: Yup Thats Mamalodi
items.summary: Elder Nelson shares a week in Mamelodi: zone leader exchanges, eight investigators at church, and a trip to the zoo.
items.body:
Matthew 10:38, 39. And he that taketh not his cross, and followeth after me, is not worthy of me. He that findeth his life shall lose it: and he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it.

This week Wednesday we went on zone leader exchanges. It was priceless to see our beloved zone leader walk through Mamelodi. He did not feel comfortable. We went to a lesson in an informal settlement. When we showed up to meet the guy (Sam), the water turned on. He said it was a miracle and we were sent from God.

This was an amazing week for sharing the gospel. We had 8 investigators show up to church, one of which was Sam! During Elders Quorum the brother giving the lesson wrote the word patience in big letters on the board and asked who had read the conference talk sent on the group chat. Nobody raised their hand. His patience immediately went out the window. Sam thought it was so funny. He said next week he would bring his family to church.

The craziest thing that happened this week was Guy Fawkes day. It is huge in Mamelodi.

Going to the zoo with my district!

Love yall,
Elder Nelson

items.subject: Transfer 3!!
items.summary: McKay shares that he got transferred to the Bitterroot YSA area as zone leader, and that a new friend accepted a baptism invitation.
items.body:
Wassup gang, so sorry its been a few weeks since my last email but there was nothing going on for a few weeks so I didn't care to write anything. ANYWAYS, transfers happened.

But before I get into that, 2 days before transfers, me and Elder Langston put someone on date! We went to visit her, her name is Sue. We had a pretty good lesson with her. After the lesson we both felt we should invite her to be baptized, so we went back to her house, Langston shared 2 Nephi 2:2 and she said "I was reading that as you knocked on my door." We asked her to be baptized and she said "I was just thinking the same thing as you two left my house earlier." The spirit was so strong. She then accepted the invitation to be baptized.

Then it was a few busy days until transfers. I got the news I'm going to the west side, to the Bitterroot YSA area! So pretty over here. My new comp is Elder Welch, who has been out about 18 months. We are the Bitterroot Zone Leaders. We also live with 2 other elders in a trailer house, super messy, and Welch and I have been cleaning it out. I love it here and I love you all! Thanks to the people who sent me the most elite Halloween packages and snacks.

Keep living it up wherever you are.

items.subject: Trust
items.summary: Elder Adamson writes from the ER after tearing his shoulder and shares thoughts on trusting God's plan and overcoming adversity.
items.body:
Why do bad things happen to us? Why is there evil in this world? Why do we have to feel pain?

First off on a positive note HAPPY BIRTHDAY TO MY BOY MAX BARTON!!! Love you.

So bad news fans, I am writing this from the ER. I tore my shoulder. Not even the most tragic thing that happened this last week. BYU lost to Utah. Hence the preceding questions.

But this has given me some time to reflect. 2 main ideas have been on my mind lately.

How do I trust in God's Plan?
How do I better overcome adversity?

Something that I KNOW is that The Book of Mormon truly does provide answers to these questions of the soul. Try it out with your own questions.

I know what God's Plan is for me. In Moses 1:39 we learn that His work and glory is to bring to pass the immortality and eternal life of us. I firmly believe that the reason I am living right now is to prepare the earth for the Second Coming of our Lord and Savior. Serving a mission is a big part of that.

Now I do not know what will happen with my shoulder. It could be another torn labrum which means surgery. It could take me out of the game for a little. But I have complete and full confidence that Nephi's words in 1 Nephi 3:7 are true. No matter what happens here with my shoulder I know that serving a mission is my commandment. Expect miracles Friends and Family. And prayers would be much appreciated.

As far as overcoming adversity, I invite you all to listen to Jon Huntsman's BYU devotional: God Did Not Put Us Here to Fail. There is opposition in all things. We need it.

Love you all,
Elder Adamson
